resolution_rule: The unified constitution and fail-closed runtime gates outrank local convenience, legacy behavior, and UI defaults.

conflicts.decision: Keep fixture mode only for synthetic tests; real mode requires SIRAJ_DESKTOP, live Qt runtime, explicit click, exact hashes, and single-use authorization.

conflicts.right: Global face prohibition and human final review
conflicts.decision: Automation may not grant final face PASS. FACE remains HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED and no critical constitutional override exists.

conflicts.right: In-video graphics and burned captions prohibited
conflicts.decision: Write only .vtt/.srt sidecars under Captions; no burned captions, title cards, lower thirds, or arbitrary graphics.

conflicts.left: Manual public title and thumbnail ownership
conflicts.decision: Manifest carries public_title=null and thumbnail=null with HUMAN ownership; internal working labels never publish automatically.
Brand directory is discovered and hash-bound for the wider SIRAJ system, but Shorts activation does not montage, alter, or copy those assets.
conflicts.authority: SR-13A storage scope and no-montage boundary

conflicts.decision: Ambiguity blocks admission. No EP001/EP002 hardcode or silent candidate selection is allowed; the user may supply a safe Video-plus-Transcript source.

conflicts.left: Existing historical certification says real episode execution NO_GO
conflicts.right: Activation certification says direct human-controlled local readiness
conflicts.decision: The historical certification remains an earlier phase record. The activation certification is scoped only to the newly implemented local Desktop workflow and does not authorize provider, paid, network, upload, or publication execution.
Tests were updated to assert the lock and zero network reachability; no skip, xfail, deletion, or safety weakening was used.

conflicts.left: Same slot receives a changed approved render
conflicts.decision: Same hash returns ALREADY_EXPORTED; changed hash receives -v2, -v3, and so on. Existing bytes are never overwritten.
Cancellation terminates the local process, removes task-owned temp output and lock, and leaves the consumed authorization non-reusable; a new explicit Desktop approval is required.
